app.name: EdgeSonic Installer
app.tagline: Deploy your own EdgeSonic instance on Cloudflare, no local tooling required.

welcome.title: Let's deploy EdgeSonic
welcome.subtitle: This wizard talks to your Cloudflare account directly from your browser and sets up a working EdgeSonic instance in a few guided steps.
welcome.freshDesc: I don't have EdgeSonic running yet. Create everything from scratch.
welcome.overwriteDesc: Recovery only. If the existing app opens, use Settings → Cloudflare → Update inside EdgeSonic instead.
welcome.requirement1: A Cloudflare account (free tier is enough to try it).
welcome.requirement2: A Cloudflare Account API Token. Optional R2 access keys enable direct playback.

overwriteAdvice.title: Use in-app update whenever possible
overwriteAdvice.message: If the existing EdgeSonic app still opens, stop this overwrite flow and use Settings → Cloudflare → Update. Overwrite deployment is only for recovery when in-app update is unavailable.

guide.title: What you'll need
guide.subtitle: Four pieces of information, all from your Cloudflare account. Here's what each one is for and how to get it — the next step is where you actually paste them in.
guide.whatAccountId: Identifies which Cloudflare account this installs into.
guide.whatApiToken: An Account API Token that lets the installer create the Worker, D1 database, and R2 bucket. Never use a Profile token for this persistent integration.
guide.whatR2Keys: The Access Key ID and Secret Access Key shown with the same Account-owned Custom Token. They enable optional R2 presigned playback.
guide.step0Desc: If you do not have a Cloudflare account, sign up with an email address and verify it. The free plan is enough to start; Cloudflare shows any billing requirement on its confirmation page. No GitHub account is needed.
guide.step1Desc: After signing in, choose the account that will own EdgeSonic. On its Account Home page, use Copy beside Account ID. The example value below is masked.
guide.accountScreenshotDetail: Account ID in the right sidebar
guide.stepR2Title: R2: enable it before creating keys
guide.stepR2Desc: In R2 Object Storage, follow the dashboard to enable R2. The installer creates the music bucket, so do not create one yourself.

optional.title: Optional features
optional.subtitle: Nothing here is required to deploy — everything below can be turned on later from inside the app too.

credentials.title: Cloudflare credentials
credentials.subtitle: The minimum API Token permissions deploy a complete working instance. Optional permissions enable advanced Cloudflare features later.
credentials.createAccount: Create or sign in to Cloudflare
credentials.setupToken: Create a Custom Token in the target account's Account API Tokens.
credentials.setupPermissions: Configure the Account API Token permissions:
credentials.dnsNotNeeded: The installer never creates or changes DNS records, so DNS Edit is not needed.

apiTokens.scenario: Read this token's policies before deployment

scripts.scenario: Deploy the Worker, assets, Secrets, and Cron

d1.scenario: Create the database and apply its schema

r2.scenario: Create and list the music bucket

accountAnalytics.scenario: In-app request, error, and CPU analytics

credentials.minimumPermissionsTitle: Minimum deployment permissions under Developer Platform
credentials.permissionAccountScope: Account resources: Include → the target account only. If the account-owned token screen only offers All accounts, use that scope.
credentials.permissionR2Scope: Optional R2 presigned playback keys: Bucket Item → Read, Include → All buckets. The bucket does not exist until deployment.
credentials.advancedPermissionsDesc: The installer stores this API Token as the Worker's CF_API_TOKEN secret. Add only the capabilities you want EdgeSonic to use from inside the app:

advancedPermissions.containers: Workers Containers → Edit — Sandbox container transcoding
advancedPermissions.observability: Workers Observability → Edit — Worker observability (not Observability Telemetry)
advancedPermissions.accountAnalytics: Account Analytics → Read — in-app request and error analytics
advancedPermissions.accountSettings: Account Settings → Read — in-app Cloudflare connection checks
advancedPermissions.zoneSettings: Zone Settings → Read — optional Images Transformations status

credentials.accountIdHelp: Found on the right sidebar of any Cloudflare dashboard page.
credentials.apiTokenHelp: Use an account-level API Token (cfat_), not a Profile API Token.
credentials.tokenGuideStep1: Open Manage Account > Account API Tokens. Do not use My Profile > API Tokens. Select Create Token.
credentials.tokenGuideStep2: For minimum deployment, set Account API Tokens to Read, then set D1, Workers R2 Storage, Workers CI, and Workers Scripts to Edit under Developer Platform.
credentials.tokenGuideStep3: Optionally add Containers, Observability, Account Analytics Read, Account Settings Read, Zone Read, and Zone Settings Read for advanced in-app features.
credentials.tokenGuideStep4: Continue to the summary and create the token. Copy the displayed Token, Access Key ID, and Secret Access Key; all three are required below.
credentials.r2KeyHelp: Optional. Add both keys to enable direct R2 presigned playback; leave both empty for normal proxied playback.
credentials.r2KeyInvalid: The R2 keys are invalid or do not have account-level R2 access.
credentials.r2KeysOptionalSkipped: Optional R2 direct-play keys were not provided; deployment can continue.
credentials.r2KeysPairRequired: Provide both R2 key fields or leave both empty.
credentials.tokenInvalid: This token couldn't be validated against account {accountId}. Double-check the token and the account ID.
credentials.r2Enabled: R2 is enabled on this account.
credentials.r2NotEnabled: R2 isn't enabled on this account yet.
credentials.r2EnableLink: Open the R2 dashboard to enable it
credentials.r2GuideStep1: Open the R2 overview page for your account below.
credentials.r2GuideStep2: Follow the dashboard to activate R2; Cloudflare shows any billing requirement before you confirm.
credentials.imagesCardDesc: Lets EdgeSonic resize cover art on demand. Not required — without it, covers are served at original size.
credentials.permissionHint: Cloudflare says this token is missing: {permission}
credentials.genericError: Something went wrong talking to Cloudflare: {message}

target.title: Deployment target
target.subtitle: Names for the Cloudflare resources this install will use. Defaults are fine for most people.
target.workerNameHelp: The name of the Cloudflare Worker running EdgeSonic.
target.bucketNameHelp: R2 bucket name — this is where uploaded music lives.
target.domainHelp: Optional. This wizard can check that the domain's zone is on your account, but binding a custom domain to the Worker currently still needs a manual step in the Cloudflare dashboard after this install finishes — the automated binding endpoint isn't wired up yet.
target.domainZoneNotFound: No zone named {domain} was found on this account. You can still continue and bind it manually later.
target.transformationsOff: Cover transformations are off. Covers still work, but thumbnails use original bytes.
target.transformationsUnavailable: Could not check cover transformations. Add Zone Settings Read to this Account API Token, or check it in Cloudflare.
target.discoveryChecking: Searching Worker, D1, and R2 resource names for EdgeSonic keywords…
target.discoveryFound: Review these keyword matches. Select the resources that belong to the existing installation.
target.discoveryNone: No Worker, D1 database, or R2 bucket with an EdgeSonic-like name was found. Verify the names before proceeding.
target.discoveryFailed: Could not search all account resources. Check the minimum token permissions and enter the names manually.
target.collisionWarning: A Worker named "{name}" already exists on this account. Since you chose fresh install, pick a different name or go back and choose overwrite instead.
target.collisionOkOverwrite: A Worker named "{name}" exists. Confirm it is the intended EdgeSonic instance before continuing.
target.overwriteMissing: No Worker named "{name}" exists. Overwrite mode cannot continue without an existing target.
target.overwriteConfirm: I verified this existing Worker and its D1/R2 names belong to the EdgeSonic installation I intend to recover.

version.title: Choose a release
version.subtitle: Pulled live from GitHub — only releases with a ready-to-deploy update package are shown.
version.sourceRepoHelp: Only change this if you're deploying from your own fork's releases.
version.localPackageHelp: Choose a ZIP containing edgesonic-update-manifest.json and edgesonic-update.tar.gz.
version.localPackageWarning: Using local package {name} ({version}). Its checksum is verified against its own manifest, but ZIP packages are not signed and cannot be confirmed as official.
version.noneEligible: No releases with a deployable update package were found for this repository.

review.title: Review before deploying
review.subtitle: Nothing has been created yet. Confirm the plan below.

execute.title: Deploying
execute.subtitle: Don't close this tab until this finishes.
execute.releaseUnavailable: The selected release is no longer available — go back and pick another.

done.saveWarning: This password is shown once and is not stored anywhere. Save it now.
done.nextStepsDesc: LastFM, email delivery, and other optional integrations aren't set up by this installer. Configure them from within EdgeSonic's own Settings after you log in, or see the secrets reference.
